Hello, listeners. Did you know there are times at night when a massive migration happens right over your heads? The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in awe. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent decades studying migratory birds, writing about them, and engaging in conservation efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr. Weidensaul.
Thanks for having me, Jo.
Your new book says every spring and fall, hundreds of millions to billions of migratory birds pass over our roofs, but we seem to have no idea that it's happening. Why is that?
Well, most birds migrate after dark, including almost all of the birds that are normally active during the day. That's why it's hard for us to realize the migration is happening. They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides, there are fewer predators at night. If you could strip away the night sky and make everything visible, this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
Among those global travelers in your book, I found the bar-tailed godwits to be particularly impressive.
Sure. Some of them can even make a 10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days.
How do they travel such a long distance over a nearly featureless ocean?
To find their routes, the bar-tailed godwits probably rely on the sun and stars among other things. Some experts believe that they may be able to sense the earth's magnetic field lines, too. You may also wonder how, if ever, they sleep while flying over a vast ocean. It turns out that migratory birds use an approach called "half-brain sleep." This is how it works. Only the left half of the brain sleeps for a couple of seconds, then only the right half for the next couple of seconds, and then this process repeats over and over again. Isn't it amazing? Actually, some sea mammals like dolphins can do that, too, because they have to keep breathing consciously.
That's a neat trick. Who wouldn't like to have such an ability?
Birds in migratory condition can do things that they can't do at other times of the year. Another neat trick you might envy is that they can gain a tremendous amount of muscle tissue without exercise. For example, before some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific, they undergo a process of binge feeding. They just eat and eat until they double their weight. By the time they take off, their heart and flight muscles may have increased by 50%. After they have eaten as much as they possibly can and can't put any more weight on, their digestive organs shrink dramatically because these won't be put to use during the non-stop flight to New Zealand.
Then what happens after they arrive there?
They regrow their digestive organs and spend the summer feeding again, and they undergo the same journey back to Alaska. They do this again and again for 25 to 30 years, flying up to 30,000 km every year. By the time bar-tailed godwits die, they have flown close to twice the distance from Earth to the moon.
That's truly impressive. By the way, I hear you've visited Korea several times before. Why do you come here so often?
As a bird watcher and conservationist, I find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and China very special. They are some of the largest tidal mudflats on the earth and provide a critical stopover point for the countless migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the human eye, they have plenty of marine life forms.
So the mudflats are drawing all kinds of birds in from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia?
Yes. Many of these birds fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. Here, they have to double their weight in less than two weeks and make another flight of several thousand kilometers up north. That's why the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It's one of the few places in the world where migratory birds can get the resources they need on their difficult journey.
Oh, I had no idea that the Yellow Sea has such importance. What do you think we can do to preserve this precious gathering place for migratory birds?
Well, you can start by raising awareness of its importance among people around you. Or, if you want to be more actively involved, you can participate in cleaning up beaches or monitoring wildlife habitats. On a bigger scale, because migratory birds travel through many countries, international cooperation is a must for their protection. Actually, I'm working with an international organization consisting of the countries along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. As a result of our international collaboration, we managed to successfully bring back the endangered black-faced spoonbills.
Fascinating! Mr. Weidensaul, today you let us see migratory birds and the Yellow Sea in a whole new way. Thank you!

det.korean: ④ less → fewer: predators는 가산명사이므로 fewer가 와야 한다. less는 불가산명사에 사용.
det.analysis:

❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ calling → called: an approach(가) called(~라고 불리는). 접근법이 '부르는' 것이 아니라 '불리는' 것이므로 과거분사 필요.
det.analysis:
❌ ② ②
✅ ① ①
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① sense: be able to + V원형 (정확). ② flying: while + V-ing 분사구문 (정확). ③ calling → called: approach가 '불리는' 것이므로 수동의 과거분사 called 필요. ④ repeats: this process(3인칭 단수) + repeats (정확).
det.tip: 현재분사 vs 과거분사: 능동(~하는) = calling / 수동(~불리는) = called. approach called X = X라고 불리는 접근법.

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ increasing → increased: may have + p.p. (현재완료) 구조이므로 과거분사 increased가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① feeding: a process of + V-ing (전치사 뒤 동명사, 정확). ② double: until they double (접속사 뒤 동사원형, 정확). ③ increasing → increased: may have + p.p. (현재완료). have increasing (X) → have increased (O). ④ dramatically: 부사로 shrink 수식 (정확).

❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④

det.korean: 큰뒷부리도요는 경로를 찾기 위해 태양과 별에 의존한다(rely on).
det.analysis:
✅ ① rely on(~에 의존하다): 경로를 찾는 수단으로 태양과 별에 의존
❌ ② give up(포기하다): 태양과 별을 포기하는 것은 맥락에 맞지 않음
❌ ③ run into(우연히 만나다): 경로 찾기와 무관
❌ ④ look down on(무시하다): 태양과 별을 무시하는 것은 비논리적

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 소중한 모임 장소를 보존(preserve)하기 위해 무엇을 할 수 있을까?
det.analysis:
✅ ③ preserve(보존하다): 해변 청소, 서식지 모니터링 등의 활동이 보전을 위한 것
❌ ① exploit(착취하다): precious(소중한) 장소를 착취하는 것은 모순
❌ ② abandon(버리다): 보전 활동 맥락에서 버리는 것은 반대
❌ ④ demolish(파괴하다): 소중한 장소를 파괴하는 것은 문맥과 반대
det.tip: preserve = conserve = protect (보존하다). preserve ↔ destroy/demolish. 'precious gathering place'가 보존 맥락의 단서

questions.stem: 대부분의 새들은 낮에 이동하기 때문에 우리가 이동을 알아차리기 쉽다.

det.korean: F: 대부분의 새들은 어두워진 후(after dark)에 이동한다. 그래서 알아차리기 어렵다(hard).
det.analysis: most birds migrate after dark → 대부분 밤에 이동. it's hard for us to realize → 알아차리기 어렵다. '낮에 이동'과 '쉽다'는 모두 본문과 반대.
det.tip: after dark = 어두워진 후 = 밤에. hard = 어려운. 지문의 반대를 묻는 F 문항.

questions.passage: You may also wonder how, if ever, they sleep while flying over a vast ocean. It turns out that migratory birds use an approach called "half-brain sleep." This is how it works. Actually, some sea mammals like dolphins can do that, too, because they have to keep breathing consciously.
questions.stem: 철새의 반뇌수면(half-brain sleep)은 뇌의 양쪽 반구가 동시에 잠드는 방식이다.

det.korean: F: 왼쪽 반구만 먼저 잠들고, 그 다음 오른쪽 반구만 잠드는 교대 방식이다. 동시에 잠드는 것이 아님.
det.analysis: Only the left half sleeps ... then only the right half → 교대로 잠든다. '동시에'가 아닌 '교대로'이므로 False.
det.tip: half-brain sleep = 반뇌수면. 한쪽씩 교대로 잠드는 방식. 돌고래도 같은 방식을 사용함 (의식적 호흡 필요).

questions.passage: They regrow their digestive organs and spend the summer feeding again, and they undergo the same journey back to Alaska. They do this again and again for 25 to 30 years, flying up to 30,000 km every year. By the time bar-tailed godwits die, they have flown close to twice the distance from Earth to the moon.
questions.stem: 큰뒷부리도요는 일생 동안 지구에서 달까지 거리의 약 두 배를 비행한다.

det.korean: T: 큰뒷부리도요가 죽을 때쯤이면 지구에서 달까지 거리의 약 두 배(close to twice the distance)를 비행한 것이다.
det.analysis: close to twice the distance from Earth to the moon → 지구에서 달까지 거리의 약 두 배. 본문과 일치하므로 True.
det.tip: close to = 거의, 약. twice the distance = 거리의 두 배. 매년 30,000km × 25~30년 = 750,000~900,000km.

questions.passage: Birds in migratory condition can do things that they can't do at other times of the year. Another neat trick you might envy is that they can gain a tremendous amount of muscle tissue without exercise. For example, before some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific, they undergo a process of binge feeding. They just eat and eat until they double their weight. By the time they take off, their heart and flight muscles may have increased by 50%. After they have eaten as much as they possibly can, their __________ shrink dramatically because these won't be put to use during the non-stop flight to New Zealand.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 논스톱 비행 중에는 사용되지 않을 소화 기관(digestive organs)이 극적으로 줄어든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ digestive organs(소화 기관): 다 먹은 후 비행 중 소화 기관을 사용하지 않으므로 줄어드는 것이 논리적
❌ ① flight muscles(비행 근육): 비행에 필요하므로 줄어들면 안 됨. 오히려 50% 증가
❌ ② magnetic senses(자기 감각): 줄어드는 대상으로 언급되지 않음
❌ ③ breathing patterns(호흡 패턴): 비행 중에도 호흡은 필요
det.tip: digestive organs = 소화 기관. 'won't be put to use during the non-stop flight'가 핵심 단서. 비행 중 먹지 않으므로 소화 기관이 불필요 → 축소

questions.passage: As a bird watcher and conservationist, I find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and China very special. They are some of the largest tidal mudflats on the earth and provide a critical stopover point for the countless migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the human eye, they have plenty of marine life forms. Many of these birds fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. Here, they have to double their weight in less than two weeks. That's why the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It's one of the few places in the world where __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: migratory birds can safely avoid all predators
tidal mudflats appear beautiful to the human eye
migratory birds can get the resources they need on their difficult journey

det.korean: 철새들이 힘든 여정에서 필요한 자원을 얻을 수 있는 세계 몇 안 되는 장소 중 하나이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 철새들이 자원을 얻을 수 있는 곳: 체중을 2주 안에 두 배로 늘려야 하고, 풍부한 해양 생물이 있다는 맥락
❌ ① 모든 포식자를 안전하게 피할 수 있는 곳: 본문에 언급 없음
❌ ③ 갯벌이 인간 눈에 아름다워 보이는 곳: featureless(특징 없어 보인다)가 원문
❌ ④ 국제 기구가 처음 설립된 곳: 본문 맥락과 무관
det.tip: 빈칸 전후의 'double their weight in less than two weeks' + 'critically important'가 단서. 자원 확보가 핵심 이유

questions.passage: Hello, listeners. Did you know there are times at night when a massive migration happens right over your heads? The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in awe. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent decades studying migratory birds, writing about them, and engaging in conservation efforts. Well, most birds migrate after dark, including almost all of the birds that are normally active during the day. They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides, there are fewer predators at night.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 새들은 낮에만 활동하고 밤에는 이동하지 않는다.
밤하늘은 낮보다 더 덥고 바람이 강하다.

det.korean: ① 대부분의 새들은 어두워진 후에 이동한다 — most birds migrate after dark.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 원문: 'most birds migrate after dark' — 대부분 어두워진 후 이동. 일치.
❌ ② 낮에만 활동: 원문은 낮에 활동하지만 밤에 이동한다고 했음. '밤에 이동하지 않는다'는 반대.
❌ ③ 밤하늘이 더 덥고: the night sky is cooler = 밤하늘이 더 시원하다. 반대.
❌ ④ 해양 생물: Weidensaul은 migratory birds(철새)를 연구한다.
det.tip: after dark = 어두워진 후. 시간 표현에 주의. cooler = 더 시원한 (calmer = 더 잔잔한).

questions.passage: Birds in migratory condition can do things that they can't do at other times of the year. Another neat trick you might envy is that they can gain a tremendous amount of muscle tissue without exercise. For example, before some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific, they undergo a process of binge feeding. They just eat and eat until they double their weight. By the time they take off, their heart and flight muscles may have increased by 50%. After they have eaten as much as they possibly can, their digestive organs shrink dramatically. They regrow their digestive organs and spend the summer feeding again, and they undergo the same journey back to Alaska. They do this again and again for 25 to 30 years.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 큰뒷부리도요는 폭식 과정에서 체중이 두 배로 늘어난다.
비행 중 사용되지 않을 소화 기관은 극적으로 줄어든다.
이륙할 때쯤 심장과 비행 근육이 100% 증가해 있다.

det.korean: ② 이륙할 때쯤 심장과 비행 근육이 100% 증가 — 원문은 50% 증가. 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 불일치: 원문 'increased by 50%' → 50% 증가. 100%가 아님.
❌ ① 일치: 'double their weight' = 체중 두 배.
❌ ③ 일치: 'digestive organs shrink dramatically' = 소화 기관 극적 축소.
❌ ④ 일치: '25 to 30 years' = 25~30년간 반복.
det.tip: 숫자 함정! 50% vs 100% — 시험에서 자주 출제되는 패턴. 원문의 정확한 수치를 확인해야 합니다.

questions.passage: Some of them can even make a 10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in ①<u>11 days</u>. To find their routes, the bar-tailed godwits probably rely on the ②<u>moon and clouds</u> among other things. Some experts believe that they may be able to sense the earth's ③<u>magnetic field</u> lines, too. It turns out that migratory birds use an approach called ④<u>"half-brain sleep."</u>
questions.stem: 위 글에서 원문과 다르게 쓰인 밑줄 친 부분을 고르시오.

det.korean: ② moon and clouds → sun and stars: 원문은 태양과 별에 의존한다고 했다. 달과 구름이 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 원문은 'the sun and stars' → 태양과 별. 'moon and clouds'로 바뀜.
❌ ① 11 days: 원문 그대로 (11일).
❌ ③ magnetic field: 원문 그대로 (자기장).
❌ ④ half-brain sleep: 원문 그대로 (반뇌수면).
det.tip: 오류찾기는 원문의 핵심 단어가 비슷하지만 다른 단어로 바뀐 것을 찾는 유형. sun/stars vs moon/clouds 대조.

questions.passage: They are some of the largest tidal mudflats on the earth and provide a critical stopover point for the countless migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the human eye, they have plenty of marine life forms. So the mudflats are drawing all kinds of birds in from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia? Yes. Many of these birds fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. Here, they have to double their weight in less than two weeks and make another flight of several thousand kilometers up north. That's why the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It's one of the few places in the world where migratory birds can get the resources they need on their difficult journey.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"too many to be counted; very many"

det.korean: countless = 셀 수 없이 많은. too many to be counted = 세기에 너무 많은.
det.analysis: countless = innumerable = too many to count. 본문에서 'the countless migratory birds'로 사용됨. 셀 수 없이 많은 철새들.
det.tip: countless = innumerable = numberless (셀 수 없이 많은). count(세다) + less(~없는) = 셀 수 없는.

questions.passage: As a result of our international collaboration, we managed to [success] bring back the endangered black-faced spoonbills. Fascinating! Mr. Weidensaul, today you let us see migratory birds and the Yellow Sea in a whole new way.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형을 변환하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 성공적으로(successfully) 멸종 위기의 검은머리저어새를 복원했다. success(명사) → successfully(부사).
det.analysis: managed to [부사] bring back: 동사 bring back을 수식하는 부사 필요. success(명사) → successful(형용사) → successfully(부사).
det.tip: success(명사) → successful(형용사) → successfully(부사). 동사를 수식하려면 부사(-ly)가 필요합니다.

questions.passage: If you could strip away the night sky and make everything visible, this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet. Among those global travelers in your book, I found the bar-tailed godwits to be particularly impressive. Sure. Some of them can even make a 10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific Ocean, __________.
questions.stem: 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. Alaska / in / days / western / Zealand / to / New / from / 11
questions.wa: from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days
accept: from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days
From western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days
from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days.
from western alaska to new zealand in 11 days
from western alaska to new zealand in 11 days.

det.korean: 서부 알래스카에서 뉴질랜드까지 11일 만에.
det.analysis: from A to B 구문 + in + 기간: from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days.
det.tip: from A to B = A에서 B까지. in + 기간 = ~만에. from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days = 서부 알래스카에서 뉴질랜드까지 11일 만에.

questions.ans: from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days

questions.passage: Hello, listeners. Did you know there are times at night when a massive migration happens right over your heads? The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in awe. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent decades studying migratory birds, writing about them, and engaging in conservation efforts. Well, most birds migrate after dark. They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides, there are fewer predators at night. If you could strip away the night sky and make everything visible, this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 철새의 대규모 야간 이동과 그 이유

det.korean: 주제: 철새의 대규모 야간 이동과 그 이유. 수십억 마리가 밤에 이동하는 규모와 이유(시원함, 잔잔한 공기, 적은 포식자)를 설명.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 철새의 야간 이동: massive migration at night + 이동 이유(cooler, calmer, fewer predators)
❌ ① 방해: 본문은 이동을 방해하는 내용이 아님
❌ ② 포식자 종류: 포식자는 이동 이유의 한 요소일 뿐
❌ ④ 다큐멘터리: 인터뷰 형식이지 촬영 기법이 아님
det.tip: 주제 = 글 전체를 관통하는 핵심 내용. 도입부에서 'massive migration at night'을 강조하고 이유를 설명하는 구조.

questions.passage: Oh, I had no idea that the Yellow Sea has such importance. What do you think we can do to preserve this precious gathering place for migratory birds? Well, you can start by raising awareness of its importance among people around you. Or, if you want to be more actively involved, you can participate in cleaning up beaches or monitoring wildlife habitats. On a bigger scale, because migratory birds travel through many countries, international cooperation is a must for their protection. Actually, I'm working with an international organization consisting of the countries along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. As a result of our international collaboration, we managed to successfully bring back the endangered black-faced spoonbills.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 개인은 철새 보호에 기여할 수 없다.
황해 갯벌은 관광 자원으로 개발해야 한다.
황해 보전을 위해 인식 제고와 국제 협력이 필요하다.

det.korean: 요지: 황해 보전을 위해 인식 제고와 국제 협력이 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 인식 제고 + 국제 협력: raising awareness + international cooperation is a must
❌ ① 완전히 복원: managed to bring back이지 '완전히 복원'이라고 단정하지 않음
❌ ② 기여할 수 없다: 개인도 해변 청소, 서식지 모니터링 등으로 기여 가능
❌ ③ 관광 자원 개발: 보전(preserve)이 목적이지 관광 개발이 아님
det.tip: 요지 = 필자가 전달하고자 하는 핵심 메시지. raising awareness(인식 제고) + international cooperation(국제 협력)이 키워드.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 본문의 표현을 활용하여 영작하시오.

"철새들은 여러 나라를 통과하여 이동하기 때문에, 국제적 협력이 그들의 보호를 위해 반드시 필요하다."

→ Because migratory birds travel through many countries, international cooperation is __________ for their protection. (조건: 2단어 사용)

det.korean: 국제적 협력이 그들의 보호를 위해 반드시 필요하다(a must).
det.analysis: 원문: 'international cooperation is a must for their protection'. a must = 반드시 필요한 것. must가 명사로 사용된 표현.
det.tip: a must = 반드시 필요한 것 (명사). 'is a must' = 반드시 필요하다. must는 조동사뿐 아니라 명사로도 쓰일 수 있다.
